extracted.intended_audience: The people of the State of New York / American citizens (readers of the Independent Journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Political/persuasive essays arguing for or against governmental structures (here: union vs disunion), aimed at influencing public opinion and policy. The text provides argument-based criteria for assessing the merits and dangers of national union versus separate confederacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: National government less likely to give just causes of war
rubrics_metrics.description: So far, therefore, as either designed or accidental violations of treaties and the laws of nations afford JUST causes of war, they are less to be apprehended under one general government than under several lesser ones, and in that respect the former most favors the SAFETY of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single national government, not subject to local peculiarities, will neither be induced to commit wrongs nor lack power/inclination to prevent or punish them. Example: several Indian hostilities were provoked by improper conduct of individual States rather than by the federal government.

rubrics_metrics.name: National government affords more security against direct unlawful violence
rubrics_metrics.description: One good national government affords vastly more security against dangers of direct and unlawful violence than can be derived from any other quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local passions and interests cause more violence in parts than in the whole; a national government is less affected by such passions and better able to restrain offending parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: National government better at amicable accommodation and settlement of disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: They (national governments) will be more temperate and cool, and... more in capacity to act advisedly than the offending State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National governments proceed with moderation and candor to extricate difficulties; acknowledgments/explanations/compensations offered by a strong united nation are often accepted where they would be rejected from a small state. Example: Genoa's humiliation to Louis XIV. shows how relative power affects acceptability of concessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inviting hostility by maintaining strong, prudent national posture
rubrics_metrics.description: The safety of the people... depends not only on their forbearing to give JUST causes of war to other nations, but also on their placing and continuing themselves in such a situation as not to INVITE hostility or insult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This situation consists in the best possible state of defense and depends on government quality, arms, and resources. Union helps produce that posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: One government can aggregate talent, uniform policy, and whole-interest diplomacy
rubrics_metrics.description: One government can collect and avail itself of the talents and experience of the ablest men... It can move on uniform principles of policy... In the formation of treaties, it will regard the interest of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national government can harmonize and extend foresight and precautions to each part; it can apply the whole's resources to defend particular parts more easily than separate governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified organization of militia and military resources increases efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: It can place the militia under one plan of discipline, and, by putting their officers in a proper line of subordination to the Chief Magistrate, will... consolidate them into one corps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy: separate militias for England, Scotland, Wales would be far less effective than a consolidated British militia. A divided America would struggle to raise and pay armies and fleets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified naval and fleet capacity is essential for national maritime strength
rubrics_metrics.description: One national government... called forth all the national means and materials for forming fleets; their prowess and thunder would never have been celebrated otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If constituent parts each had separate navies, they would dwindle into insignificance. Applied to America: division prevents formation of powerful fleets and carrying trade advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division creates command, coordination, and provisioning difficulties in joint defense
rubrics_metrics.description: How, and when, and in what proportion shall aids of men and money be afforded? Who shall command the allied armies?... Who shall settle the terms of peace, and in case of disputes what umpire shall decide between them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple sovereigns produce inseparable difficulties and inconveniences for combined defense; a single government avoids these embarrassments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign powers will treat states according to perceived unity and competence
rubrics_metrics.description: But whatever may be our situation... foreign nations will know and view it exactly as it is; and they will act toward us accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the national government is efficient, well administered, trade prudently regulated, militia disciplined, finances discreetly managed, and people united, foreign nations will favor friendship; if divided or weak, they will scorn or exploit us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division into confederacies invites foreign manipulation and partial alignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of [the confederacies] would have its commerce with foreigners to regulate by distinct treaties... different commercial concerns must create different interests, and of course different degrees of political attachment to and connection with different foreign nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would likely produce foreign powers taking different sides among American confederacies, making united defense harder and enabling foreign influence and conquest under the guise of alliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neighboring independent states tend toward jealousy, distrust, and mutual injury
rubrics_metrics.description: They would neither love nor trust one another, but on the contrary would be a prey to discord, jealousy, and mutual injuries; in short, they would place us... FORMIDABLE ONLY TO EACH OTHER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples: former divisions of Britain and other countries show neighboring states often embroiled in quarrels; union reduces internal rivalries and jealousies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial republics are not inherently more peaceful; commerce shifts motives for war
rubrics_metrics.description: Has commerce hitherto done anything more than change the objects of war?... Sparta, Athens, Rome, and Carthage were all republics... Yet were they as often engaged in wars, offensive and defensive, as the neighboring monarchies of the same times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial interests produce rivalries in trade and navigation that have often led to war; commerce alone does not guarantee peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vicinity (nearness) tends to make nations natural enemies absent confederation or constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Vicinity or nearness of situation, constitutes nations natural enemies unless their common weakness forces them to league in a confederate republic, and their constitution prevents the differences that neighborhood occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation frames the problem (evil) and points to the remedy (union/constitution) for neighborly jealousy and conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial disputes among states are a fertile source of hostility and require central arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: Territorial disputes have at all times been found one of the most fertile sources of hostility among nations... We have a vast tract of unsettled territory... A dismemberment of the Confederacy... would revive this dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized authority (the Union) has been used to settle cessions and manage western territory; dissolution would reopen claims, create contention over apportionment, and make the sword likely to decide differences.
